newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday December 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday December 5.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Centre-right opposition has decided to continue to boycott votes in parliament on the 1997 budget, refusing to take part in debate sessions in the Upper House (Senate) as long as the government does not drop its request for special powers that will allow the cabinet to legislate on some areas of fiscal policy without recourse to parliament. (all).
* Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti met with Prime Minister Romano Prodi, after which he said "I am ready to bet nobody is going to touch pensions next year" (all).
* The Bologna headquarters of Nomisma, a research and counselling company founded by Prodi, was searched by the police in an inquiry over alleged bribes concerning high-speed railways (all).
* The anti-Mafia parliamentary commission elected pro-government politician Ottaviano Del Turco as its new chairman (all).
* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said Italy would do its best to join the first group of countries launching the European single currency in 1999 (all).

* Mobile phone group Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) has asked the Italian Post Ministry for authorisation to offer a cordless phone service. TIM's sister company Telecom Italia in October had announced plans to launch an advanced cordless phone using the Digital European Cordless Telephony (DECT) standard (all).

* European Commission inspectors are expected to arrive in Rome over the weekend to discuss with the Treasury the sale of a 60 percent stake in ailing Banco di Napoli. A European source reportedly said the EU has doubts about Banco di Napoli being taken over by a state-owned bank (all).
* Labour minister Tiziano Treu is due to meet today metal workers and engineering trade unions and employers to discuss contract renewals (all).

* Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani called a new meeting with Olivetti managers and trade unions on December 18 to discuss the crisis of at the information technology group. A PDS party note said the government must "promote negotiations on the future of the group, which must be global" . The PDS is the largest political grouping in the centre-left government (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
